utterances.text: I don't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today you were shown a number of statements by the Prosecutor, which belong to Exhibit P386. I think you have these documents before you. Mr. Eric, would you please take a look at what ought to be the statement of Veselin Sarac. You told us today -- or, rather, you confirmed to us today that what should be a statement of Veselin Sarac given to the court bears your signature.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that you never examined this person as investigating judge but, rather, that that was done by Pavle Jelisavcic, called Paja.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Pavle Jelisavcic quite obviously was not a judge of the basic court in Zvornik, nor was he -- nor did he work for them as a contractor.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No, he did not work for the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I want you once again to take a look at this statement. It says here that the record of the witness examination was compiled on the 25th of August, 1994, before the investigating judge Vaso Eric. You have already told us that this is not true.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, I did say that this was not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the criminal legal system of the former Yugoslavia as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina before the war and during the war and until recently, such examinations were not recorded on audiotapes or videotapes except in special circumstances and cases regulated by the law; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is why the record of the witness hearing or the record from a hearing were of crucial importance in our legal system?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Law on Criminal Procedure of the former Yugoslavia had special provisions regulating in very specific terms how records should be compiled and signed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The recording clerk is a person compiling the record who always had to verify the veracity or the accuracy of the records by their signature; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at the record of a witness examination. It's page bearing the number 02113315, and the bit where it says that -- that has the name of Gorica Trajkovic. She, in fact, never signed this record; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because we've lost you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've lost you, Madam Vidovic. Forgive me if I'm making a mistake, but going through -- browsing through the statements that we have here, I see none bearing the ERN number 02113315. They all start with 0260. Correct me if I am wrong, or direct me to the right document anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I was trying to be as brief as possible, so I crossed out a lot of my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at the number 0306282. Page 7 in the Bosnian version. So the number is 0360282. What I asked, Mr. Eric, was that regardless of who the recording clerk in this instance was, he or she did not sign the record?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: That's right. It wasn't signed by the recording clerk, and the recording clerk ought to sign the record. You are absolutely right about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in 1994 in Republika Srpska, the Criminal Code that was adopted from the former Yugoslavia was applied with some slight amendments.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The competence and jurisdiction of the investigating judge were not in fact altered or affected by those amendments?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please? I would like to place on the ELMO the following document, extract from the Law on Criminal Procedure. I will be showing some of these to the witness, asking him to comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the Law on Criminal Procedure that was published in Dr. Spiro Vukovic's book in 1985. If you could please look at Article 161. It was published in Belgrade, and the page number is 128. I will now quote paragraph 1 of Article 161. Witness, hold on a moment. I haven't found it yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, if you could look at this, the Law on Criminal Procedure, the title page, and then if you could go page by page all the way to page 128. Right there in the middle you will find Article 161. I hope I've been of assistance to you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed you have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, can you please look at Article 161. I'm quoting paragraph 1 to you now. It reads: "The investigation shall be conducted by the investigating judge of the competent court." Paragraphs 2 and 3 talk about the local jurisdiction of the -- territorial jurisdictions of the courts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, any investigation can only be carried out by the investigating judge upon a request by the prosecutor with jurisdiction over the case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in this specific case there was no investigation to begin with, because no further steps were taken after these statements were collected.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Eric. We'll come to at that later. Can you now please look at Article 156. In relation to this, you were asked a question by the president. Today, you have tried to explain that it is quite possible for an investigating judge before the criminal procedure is started to take statements. I'm now showing you Article 156. This is something quite different. I will read to you what it says. Paragraph 1: "The investigative judge of the competent court and the investigative judge of a lower court within whose jurisdiction a crime was committed may take certain investigative actions if to postpone those actions would entail risks even before a decision to conduct an investigation has been made, but the public prosecutor with jurisdiction over the case must be informed about all the actions taken." Mr. Eric, it is true, isn't it, that the investigating judge could only take these steps when the case was urgent, for example, on-site inspections and investigations, the risk of death and other such cases? Would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Statements taken in this way would then be entered into the criminal investigation file, Kri file?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it's true, isn't it, that you as an investigating judge, in every case you handled had to inform the public prosecutor with jurisdiction over the case on every step and every little thing you did in relation to the case?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This specific investigation, number 74/94, that's how the document is marked, we are speaking about what is purportedly a statement made by Veselin Sarac. You never, in fact, informed the public prosecutor about this; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a number assigned to this excerpt on the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But can you please keep the document, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document being tendered by the Defence is being admitted and marked as Defence Exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 196. MR. DI FAZIO: That the entirety of -- the entirety of what has been handed out, if Your Honours please, or is it purely and simply part of it? I've got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are only excerpts from -- I take it these are part from -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, a bundle of extracts. That's the whole exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I so they. That's the way I understood it. MR. DI FAZIO: I just wanted to be clear about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I will require this document on perhaps two further occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, the public prosecutor never proposed that you should entrust the -- any agencies of the Ministry of the Interior with these actions pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nor did -- nor was Pavle Jelisavcic ever an authorised official of the Ministry of the Interior, was he?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, what you told us today was that Pavle Jelisavcic had had an authorisation from the Ministry of Justice of Republika Srpska. I'm putting it to you that even if Jelisavcic had been authorised by anyone at all, including the Government of Republika Srpska, to gather information, evidence, take statements, I'm putting it to you that he could not have done this using a form printed by the Zvornik Municipal Court. Would I not be right in claiming that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I said that I'd phoned the Ministry of Justice of Republika Srpska and spoken to someone who was either deputy or assistant minister, the person named Goran Neskovic. This person told me that there was an agreement to the effect that Pavle Jelisavcic was authorised to take these statements. I acted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Eric, you were a sworn judge of the Zvornik court. You were bound to follow the letter of the law. The government had nothing whatsoever to do with this, did they?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: In the case at hand, I listened to what Goran Neskovic told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That much is clear. In any case, Mr. Jelisavcic, even if he took those statements, could only have done it under his own authority and under his own name. Do you not agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I think this actually is the case, but I at the time received different information from the Ministry of Justice. At the time, as I say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask you a different set of questions now. In actual fact, when you signed those statements, you had no idea whether those people had been cautioned to tell the truth and told about the possible consequences of perjury?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I had no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you don't know at all whether these statements were in their entirety suggested to these people?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know if each and every person was interviewed separately and individually as provided for by the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, it's true, isn't it, that under the law, there was no way that as a judge in Zvornik you would have been allowed to sign statements made by people you'd never even seen or known that they in fact existed?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: That is true. However, at the time I believed both Pavle Jelisavcic and Goran Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavle Jelisavcic and his Belgrade commission did not only interview witnesses in this way in the territory of Republika Srpska, did they? They also gathered other kinds of evidence including different kinds of documents, reports of on-site investigations, autopsy reports, photographs, audio and videotapes. Would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. I only know about these statements. I don't know about anything else that Pavle did, because he never discussed anything with me. If this is the case, it's not something that I can deny, but I have no personal knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now remind you of something. Do you agree with me when I say that exhumation and autopsy are two things that would fall under sole jurisdiction of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please look at the excerpt, Article 154 on the Law on Criminal Procedure. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will read now what Article 2 -- paragraph 2, Article 154 says. This is the Law on Criminal Procedure that was in force in Republika Srpska at the time. It reads: "If the investigative judge is unable to reach the scene of crime immediately, internal affairs agencies upon the approval of the investigating judge may themselves conduct an inquest on the spot and order necessary expert evaluations with the exception of autopsy and exhumation of the corpse."

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we agree that these steps could only be taken by an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at Article 253 on the Law on Criminal Procedure. I will quote Article 253. It's a brief one. It reads: "When an expert is not carrying out his functions in a professional institution, the examination of the body and the autopsy shall be conducted by one, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. two, or several doctors when necessary, preferably specialised in forensic medicine. An investigating judge shall direct these activities by experts' teams and the findings and opinions of the experts shall be recorded in the minutes." It is true, isn't it, that an autopsy report or an exhumation report would -- could only have been performed or done by an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It would have been under his jurisdiction to describe the condition of the body, any items of clothing or any other objects or implements found next to the body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under the law, the investigating judge would be bound to gather all these items, all this evidence, which would then constitute part of the criminal report, would it not?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You in fact attended the exhumation of a body that was purportedly the body of Kostavin [phoen] Popovic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, but person in charge of that exhumation was investigating judge Zoran Dimitric, not myself. I merely accompanied them on the occasion, and I did nothing, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that neither you nor Zoran Dimitric ever drew up an exhumation report including a description of the body, items found near the body, persons who identified the body, manner or method of identification or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: This could only have been done by this particular judge, Zoran Dimitric. I was not involved with that particular exhumation at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, isn't it in fact unusual for two Judges to attend an exhumation, neither of them writing a report which is their jurisdiction and no one else's?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: There's been a misunderstanding between us. I wish to clarify this. I did not attend this exhumation at all, nor was I supposed to write a report. The person in charge of this exhumation was the investigating judge Zoran Dimitric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that he never wrote that report on exhumation?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that. I can't claim that. If he didn't, he should have written it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I will turn to something else. You stated that it was you who personally interviewed certain persons in 1994 pursuant to the request of the prosecutor in relation to the criminal complaint against Naser Oric. You said that these people testified about certain events taking place in villages around Srebrenica and Bratunac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the requests of the basic public prosecutor in Zvornik and his proposals, it is possible that I interviewed some persons, because in the request to conduct an investigation, the names of these persons were listed down as the names of witnesses, and I was the one who scheduled the investigative hearings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely what I mean. In addition to the criminal complaint against Naser Oric or request to conduct an investigation against Naser Oric, would you say that there were other such investigations? I didn't hear your answer. Was it a yes or not? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to one case only, one criminal complaint only, or to others as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question so that it is more clear. I think that there were several criminal complaints against Muslim perpetrators, including the complaint against Naser Oric. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. There were several such complaints.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All of these cases had to be registered in the court registration books where criminal investigations were registered or recorded and which is marked as Ki registry book?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and they were registered there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that all statements that you have seen here today that were shown to you by the prosecutor, including the one of Veselin Sarac, are marked with Kri?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I with like the usher to put another statement before you. This is Prosecutor's Exhibit P406.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will give another statement to the usher, the statement of Slavka Matic, because I'm going to put identical questions in relation to these two statements. MR. DI FAZIO: May I just see D406, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, please take a look at the statement of Stanisa Stevanovic, the first page of that statement, just the first page, and then please take a look at the statement of Slavka Matic, first page again. Do you agree with me that both of these statements, we are now referring to the Bosnian version, not the translation, so the original Bosnian version, Mr. Eric. Do you have it? Do you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I have just one statement in front of me, the statement of Stanisa Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Within the one we have is the one of Slavka Matic. This is not marked as an exhibit, as yet at least. If it is already an exhibit, we must be extremely careful that we don't mix one with the other. What does the witness have? Because obviously the witness has a statement which actually you referred, which we don't have here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you remember the testimony of Stanisa Stevanovic, we discussed it for quite a long time, and at one point you asked whether that statement would be tendered as either the Prosecutor's or Defence's exhibit, and the Prosecutor, I think Mr. Di Fazio, asked that it be tendered as the Prosecutor's exhibit, and in accordance with our records, it was assigned number P406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are wasting time. You have not understood me. I'm not saying that the statement of Stanisa Stevanovic does not exist or that it has not been tendered. I am saying that it seems the witness has been given that statement and is being asked questions upon it while we were given a statement which is not yet marked, at least what I have here, a statement I have here, a statement by Slavka Martic. So first we must agree that we are talking about two statements. Do you want to put to the witness two statements or just one statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both of the statements simultaneously, because it's just one topic we're going to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. This second statement, that is the one of Slavka Matic, has it been given a number already?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I'm going to request that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we're on the same wave length. So you may ask the question, and you've got five minutes before we break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, I hope you had a chance to take a look at both of the statements?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I saw just one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the number in the upper-right corner. So please take a look at the statement of Stanisa Stevanovic. Do you agree that it is marked Ki 64/93?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you then agree that the statement of Slavka Matic is also marked 69/93?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you then agree that these statements were taken in a regular court investigating procedure?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: I couldn't state that with certainty right now because it is possible that there was a mistake here and that Ki was not crossed out and marked Kri. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that. Now please turn to the last page of both statements. Would you agree that the recording clerk signed both of these statements?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean anything to you, Mr. Eric?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: However, the recording Aleksandra Cvetkovic, was never an employee of the court in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is it possible that even when it comes to regular legislation books in court, which are very formal documents in our system, that these statements were recorded there?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No. They could not have been. If we are dealing with Ki statements, then these statements are recording only in individual case files, and they represent an integral part of that case file.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, is it possible -- was it possible for such mistakes to occur? Is it possible that a wrong registration number was assigned?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Well, mistakes are possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that something of that nature is not possible, but we will turn to something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So there will be 197, D197.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I just make a quick point for the English transcript. My colleague referred on a number of occasions to the -- to the purported statement of Veselin Sarac and on one occasion it was translated as "what ought to be the statement of Veselin Sarac," on another occasion "as what should be the statement of Veselin Sarac." I'm looking at page 47 of the transcript. In fact the correct interpretation should be: "What is purportedly the statement of Veselin Sarac." And certainly that's our position. It's not the statement of Sarac, it's only purportedly his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point taken. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's continue and finish, please, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I decided to skip putting many of the questions I had initially planned, and instead of that will put only one more or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Madam Vidovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eric, you were shown the decision to conduct an investigation against Naser Oric and a number of other people, number Ki 81/93. This is OTP Exhibit P492. Do you remember seeing this decision and commenting upon it?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained that an investigation was conducted against Naser Oric for a war crime against civilian population under the Criminal Code of 142 of Republika Srpska, which is identical to the Article 142 of the Criminal Code of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. This law was adopted in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that that was one of the most serious crimes in our criminal legislation?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the law prescribed the most severe punishment for this crime.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in a case such as this, a suspect was entitled to have Defence counsel to represent him and also other suspects in this case, that this was a mandatory provision, meaning that there ought to have been a Defence counsel appointed?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. However, he was not interviewed, and that's why no Defence counsel was appointed. However, you are right. In such cases, this is a mandatory provision that there be a Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in a case such as this one, no steps should have been taken without the presence of Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Defence counsel was never appointed to represent Naser Oric or anybody else in this case in the course of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. No Defence counsel was ever appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Is there re-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Brydensholt from Denmark would like to put a question to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Regarding this decision which has just been discussed, which ended up deciding that all the 27 suspects should be put on pre-trial detention or arrest. Was there at all any examination of witnesses or any investigation going on before that decision was taken or was it just taken when the accusations were presented to you?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: This decision was adopted pursuant to the request by the prosecutor. There were no interviews before this decision was taken. No interviews were conducted by the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a very simple question, and again it's -- you told me earlier on -- you told us earlier on that when Pavle Jelisavcic came to your office, Gorica Trajkovic was with him.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Pavle gave you all these statements for you to sign.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you signed them.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you knew at the time, I'm sure, that according to the law, they should have also been signed by the recording clerk.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that, but I didn't pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If she was present there with this Pavle Jelisavcic, why didn't you ask her to sign?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I simply failed to bear that in mind at the time. The established practice is not that you should remind the recording clerk to sign the record of a statement. It is a recording clerk's duty to do it without being prompted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the last question: This Pavle, what was his background? Was he a policeman? Was he a lawyer? What was his experience, I mean, and occupation? Do you know? Did you inquire?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: He told me that he was there on behalf of the committee, and he was a lawyer by profession. That was what he told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question with regard to the timing of these documents. The decision on contacting the investigation dates of January 19, 1994, and these investigations made by this Pavle date from August or December 1994. Now, is there a relation between your decision on conducting the investigation and that later on this investigation was conducted by Pavle? Yes. I don't remember now, but you know whom we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: No, there is no relation whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Last question: In the explanation of your decision at the end it would say: "From the information contained in the document, there is reasonable suspicion that the accused, and accomplices, committed the criminal act..." Now, if you go through this decision there are only events described but it's difficult to see any evidence put forward to see these allegations. Now, what is meant by "information contained in the document as basis for this decision."

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: This is a perfectly common sentence, very common phrasing in investigations. You usually say that there are reasonable grounds to suspect, but this does not in itself mean that anything yet has been proven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Brydensholt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Not that it has not been proven, but do you remember, was there at all any documentation presented to you? You told me earlier that you didn't hear any evidence or made any investigation yourself, but were you at all presented by any documents which seemed to indicate to indicate that the accused was guilty?

utterances.speaker: VASO ERIC
utterances.text: Aside from the criminal complaint, there were certain interviews, and then there was a request to conduct an investigation, a request made by the prosecutor. It was based on those documents, as was normally the case, that an investigation was initiated. At a later stage during the proceedings, the guilt of the accused was to be proven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That brings us to the end of your testimony, Mr. Eric. On behalf of Judge Brydensholt from Denmark, Judge Eser from Germany and myself, my name by the way is Judge Carmel Agius and I come from Malta, I wish to thank you for having to accepted to come over and give testimony in this case. I know it couldn't have been a pleasant experience for you, but I wish to thank you. And on behalf of the Tribunal, I want to assure you that you will receive all the assistance you require to facilitate your return back home. I would like to say that the two parties Prosecution and Defence did their utmost to finish with your testimony today and not keep you here for the weekend because tomorrow we will not be sitting. We have other business to transact, and that would have meant you staying over the entire weekend and resuming on Monday. So I wish to express my gratitude to both Mr. Di Fazio and Madam Vidovic for having cooperated and made it easier for the witness to return, made it possible for the witness to return back home early.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On behalf of everyone present here, I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we will -- tomorrow, as you know, no sitting. I will have a long sitting tomorrow, but not you. We will then reconvene on Monday. So Monday's sitting will be Courtroom II in the afternoon. Thank you. Have a nice evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.32 p.m.,
